check: Uses the simplest design that fits ~2 KB of policies: the policies go into the prompt (or a trivial deterministic retrieval), with no vector database, embeddings pipeline or agent framework. Justifying the choice counts in its favour; heavy infrastructure fails this.
Answers are tied to sources: the prompt or code requires citing the policy file or section the answer came from.
When the policies don't answer the question, the agent says so and points to HR, rather than answering from general knowledge (explicit instruction and/or handling).
The work states what 'good' means for this agent (e.g. accurate, cited, abstains when unsure, scope limited to these policies), in code docs, a doc file or the final message.

There is an eval set of questions with expected answers or sources, including at least one unanswerable question and some tricky specifics (carry-over limit, 3-day medical certificate, NZD 500 approval).
Tests run offline with a fake model and pass.
Puts the static policy text in a cacheable prefix (prompt caching / cache_control) or otherwise addresses the repeated per-question cost of sending all policies.
The final message is accurate about what was verified (no live model run) and what to do next to know it works.
